claim: AC-9 and AC-10 fix the labels of the attention and steps lines but not which of the six numbers appear, in what order and format, nor the layout of the measure output; two builders would print different lines and both pass the criteria.

The term Event gives a wait but no time, while the Window selects events by their time; a dialog whose call lies before the cursor and whose result lies after it is counted twice or never, depending on the choice.
AC-6 says the stop or the session-end hook passes the 10-minute rule of STP-26; in the code only the stop reach has that rule, and the Session end row of the Test plan contradicts the criterion.

For stop the window end is the end of its token window, which is exclusive when a later message has the same time; an event at exactly that time is counted now and passed over later, or dropped; a stop with no complete message has no end and the spec does not say what is written.
AC-5 skips a result whose call is not in the file, and the Sums row of the Test plan gives a result before its call a wait of 0; for a result line that precedes its call line the two disagree.

The wall time rule differs between Design (the earliest from of any record, to closed.at) and the Report row of the Test plan (attention records, to the latest to); a close before the earliest from gives a negative time; the report without a key is not specified.

A dialog's wait runs to the result, so it holds the tool's run time (an approved test run of 9 minutes counts as 9 minutes of attention), and parallel calls of one message each count the same period, so attention is summed over overlapping periods.

Other user lines pass the test of AC-3: the compaction summary line and the lines that say a request was interrupted by the user; each would count as a typed message, the first with the whole gap as its wait; two typed lines in a row count the same period twice.

Some Plan steps name tests that pass before the code: the subagent guard of step 3, the unchanged report of step 5, the repeat of step 4 under the 10-minute rule; the RED of step 7 removes a case from the old test, which cannot make it fail.

The steps come from the first-parent history of HEAD; after the merge of a parallel ticket's branch by a merge commit its step commits are not on that history, and the report on main shows 0 steps for every such ticket.

The whole window of events goes to one target ticket; a session that serves several tickets in turn puts every dialog and question of the window on the ticket that is current when the hook runs, and the ticket does not list this.

AC-11 says the error line names the path, but the case without an argument has no path; a test of a file without read permission fails when the suite runs as root; a FIFO and a link loop are not listed.

The at of an attention record counts for the 10-minute rule, so an attention record alone makes the next stop wait before it writes token records; the guarantee that the token records are unchanged is not exact.
No time or memory bound is stated for the second full read of a transcript of tens of MB in the hooks and in measure.
measure is silent on subagent files that name another session, files of another name in the folder, a last message without a final line, and the wall time of a file with fewer than two timed lines.

note: AC-9 gives the exact attention line and steps line; AC-10 gives the layout of the measure output
the term Event defines its time (the result or the line) and its interval; the Cursor row tests a cursor between a call and its result
AC-6 gives the 10-minute rule to stop only
the attention window is not bound by the token window; to is the time of its last event; a stop with no complete message writes an attention record alone
one pass: a result whose call is not on an earlier line is skipped (AC-5); the Sums row tests a result timed before its call
one wall time rule in AC-13: the earliest from to the latest to of the ticket's attention records; AC-9 covers the report without a key
the times are the union of the events' intervals, so parallel calls count once (AC-4, Sums row); the tool's run time inside a dialog's wait is listed as not promised, an upper bound cut by the cap
AC-3 leaves out the compaction summary and the interrupt lines; typed lines in a row count once by the union

every pair names tests that fail at its RED; the three tests that pass at once are coverage steps 3b, 4b and the repeat uses session-end; step 6 changes the old test's case so that it fails at the RED
the steps are the distinct labels among the commits reachable from HEAD, merge commits followed (AC-13), with a test on a merged history
the human widened the promise on 2026-11-11: the events of one call are split by the worktree folder of their lines (promise item 7, AC-15, step 3d)
AC-11 names the usage text for the call without FILE; the Bad files row adds a FIFO and tests the unreadable file as hook_tokens does
the Guarantees say that the content of the token records is unchanged and list the delay of up to 10 minutes after an attention record alone as not promised
the Guarantees state that the reader streams the file and holds one line and the ids of the calls
AC-10 and the Measure row name the subagent files that count, the partial last message and the wall time of one timed line
